notes.decision: Coptic numeral ϥ̄ = 90. Marks Kephalaion 90. The triple ϥ̄ in lines 17-19 frames the chapter heading typographically (centered above, then opening and closing the title-block in line 19).

Translated 'the Ten Ways'. ⲙⲛⲧⲏ = Lyc. variant of ⲙⲏⲧ '10' with prosthetic ⲛ̄ and final ⲏ. Note: the body-text describes 4 + 8 = 12 ways, with arithmetic tension; the heading's 'ten' is likely the round/canonical count of ways treated, while the body subdivides further (4 to light, 8 mingled, of which subgroups go to Gehenna or transmutation).

ⲛⲁⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ = future of ⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'go forth, escape' (in glossary). ⲁⲧⲉ here functions as negative-purpose conjunctive 'lest, so that not'. The catechumen escapes precisely so his wealth does NOT go to Gehenna by the three (bad) ways.

notes.coptic_form: ⲙⲛⲧⲏ ⲙⲙⲁⲓⲧ ⲛⲉⲧⲥⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ
notes.decision: 'Ten ways which draw forth from the Zone' — the cosmic Zone (zodiacal girdle) is the source from which all the ways of fate/destiny extend. The catechumen's wealth, like souls, traverses these ways. Manichaean cosmology of the Zone as conduit (cf. accumulated ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ).
'Four ways which are chosen, which are reckoned' — the upward soteriological paths to life. ⲥⲁⲧϩ qualitative of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ 'be chosen, elect'. ⲏⲡ qualitative of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, belong'.

Tentatively parsed as ⲉⲩⲭⲓ ⲁ-ⲡⲡⲉ 'going up to the height' + ⲭⲛ̄ (Lyc. = ϫⲓⲛ 'from') + ⲙⲡⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ 'from that place.' The eight mingled ways extend upward; from that height, the light-portion is then drawn upward to the ships while the error-portion is cast down. Reading ⲡⲡⲉ as 'the height' is uncertain; alternative: ⲡⲡⲉⲭⲛ̄ as a single noun (unidentified locus).

notes.coptic_form: ⲛϩⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧⲟⲩ ⲛϩⲥⲱⲧϥ̄ ⲛϩⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ
notes.decision: Three coordinated conjunctive verbs describing the light's extraction: 'going forth from them (the mingled ways), being rescued, going within (= unto the ships).' Each ⲛ̄ϩ- is the Lyc. conjunctive prefix.

Greek μετάλλισμος / μεταλλαγμός 'transmutation, transmigration' (cf. accumulated ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ). Refers to metempsychosis: souls mingled with Error are subjected to rebirth-cycles before final consignment.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ⲉⲧⲏⲡ ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ ⲛⲉⲧⲥⲏⲕ ⲁⲛⲅⲉⲉⲛⲛⲁ
notes.decision: 'The three ways which are reckoned to the Error are those that draw (one) down to Gehenna.' This is the Elect's own restatement of Mani's prior teaching (after the leer) before posing his actual question, which presumably continues on the next page.

Translated 'drawn' throughout this kephalaion. The verb ⲥⲱⲕ here governs the cosmic-soteriological motion of souls being pulled either to Gehenna (downward, by the three ways) or to the country of the Living (upward). Its repeated occurrence makes it the structural verb of the chapter.

Translated 'abundance' consistently. The threefold formula ⲡϩⲁϣϩⲱ̄ ⲛ̄- enumerates the three categories of sin (lawlessness/killings/wounding-words) that draw the catechumen to Gehenna. The repeated 'abundance' captures both the multitude and intensity of these acts.

Translated 'his corpses' / 'his burials'. ⲕⲉⲉⲥ here is Lycopolitan reflex of either ⲕⲁⲥ 'bone' or ⲕⲱⲱⲥ 'burial preparation, corpse'. In the context (replacing ⲁⲛⲟⲙⲓⲁ in the threefold structure that originally was lawlessness/killing/wounding-word, where ⲡⲟⲣⲛⲓⲁ has now substituted for lawlessness), the third category here corresponds to killing (ϩⲱⲧⲃⲉ from line 3). 'Corpses/burials' as metonym for killings preserves the metonymic register: the man's heaps of dead/buried victims are the visible residue of his killing-acts.

Translated 'the metallagmos of Gehenna' — Greek μεταλλαγμός 'transmutation/exchange.' This is Manichaean polemical vocabulary for metempsychosis/transmigration (cf. accumulated ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ). The pre-baptismal sins of the catechumen continue to draw him into transmigratory bondage (line 19: 'following after their members unto bondage').
Greek πάντῃ πάντως 'altogether by all means' — strong adverbial intensifier. Translated 'altogether-by-all-means' to preserve the doubled emphatic.

ⲕⲁⲧⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ rendered 'against me' — the elect speaker reflects on the gravity of metempsychosis as it touches his own situation/concern. ⲧⲟⲛⲱ taken as adverbial intensifier 'exceedingly' (split across lines 20-21), modifying ⲙⲁⲭϩ̄ 'hard' — 'the matter is exceedingly hard for him to live.'

Following leer-marker. Read as ⲁⲧⲟ⟨ⲛ⟩ = ⲁⲧⲱⲛ 'to where' with elision of final ⲛ — completing the disciple's question 'their end shall arrive at where?' The leer marks intentional pause before Mani's answer at line 25. Marked with angle brackets to indicate scribal omission rather than gap.

Translated 'that they may be chosen for their forms.' ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ here is passive-causative 'be chosen, be selected' with ⲛ̄- introducing the form-allocation. The Manichaean pre-incarnational doctrine: souls of elect and catechumens-of-faith are pre-elected to their cosmic forms in the Height before being begotten in the flesh. Alternative reading 'that they may receive their forms' is also possible if ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ is read in the Lyc. extended sense.

Translated as 'he habitually chooses' — Lyc. habitual prefix ϣⲁϩ- (= Sah. ϣⲁϥ-) + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'choose.' The habitual aspect captures the apostle's iterative cosmic-ecclesial activity of selecting forms in each new community.

Double appositive 'that is the Elect, that is the Catechumens' specifies the two grades constituting the 'freemen' of the Church — the standard Manichaean two-fold ecclesiastical structure (electi and auditores).

Read as ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧⲟⲩ ('from-them') with Lyc. ⲉⲓ for ⲏ; the freemen status applies to both Elect and Catechumens. Alternative reading 'and bringing them' (conjunctive of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ) is possible but less idiomatic in context.

Lyc. conjunctive ⲛ̄ϥ-ϭⲛ-ⲧⲟⲩ 'and-he-finds-them' (ⲁⲛ for ϭⲛ). The descent to find people in 'peoples and peoples' and 'heresies and heresies' is the apostolic mission of choosing forms from variegated worldly contexts.

'Having attained him in a transformation' — the catechumens attain the apostle through the transformative event of conversion. ⲕⲁⲧⲁⲛⲧⲉ (Greek καταντάω) is the eschatological verb 'arrive at' (cf. glossary).
ⲡⲥ-|ⲁⲩⲛⲉ across line break = ⲡⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'the knowledge.' The pair 'seal of faith and knowledge sealed upon his soul' is the soteriological signature that protects the catechumen.
Begins the parable: 'the manner of a horse of (a) king (which is sealed)' — the royal-horse-with-seal analogy that occupies lines 14-17, paralleling the catechumen-with-seal in lines 17-25.

Translated 'carry off' (theft sense) — the verb fits the parable context of stealing a sealed royal horse. Likely Lyc. variant of ϣⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'plunder, seize' or related martial-acquisition root. Confidence moderate; could alternatively be ϣⲱⲧⲣ̄ 'yoke' (harness for theft).

Parsed as Lyc. habitual ϣⲁⲥ- (3sg.f.) + a verb of trust/reliance (likely from ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'trust' or ⲱⲛϩ-stem) + 3sg.m suffix + ⲁⲭⲱϩ 'upon him.' The form (the catechumen's heavenly form) trusts in the catechumen below and protects him from defilement. Confidence moderate; verbal stem uncertain.
ⲥⲱⲕ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲧⲉ idiom: 'draw together / draw with one another' — the catechumens are drawn through the transformation collectively, with the toil and the angels' purification.

ⲙⲉⲧⲉ here = 'fellowship, agreement, together' (cf. ⲥⲱⲕ ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲧⲉ in segment 28); 'the hour of fellowship' = the gathered/communal hour of ecclesial conversion-purification. Distinct from homophonous ⲙⲉⲧⲉ 'consent.'

Rendered 'giving-of-fear' preserving the verbal idiom ϯ + ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ ('give fear,' i.e. fear of God). The compound parallels ϯⲣⲉⲛ 'give a name' and similar idioms; the noun ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ = ϩⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (cf. accumulated tentative entry ⲍⲟⲩⲗⲧⲉ).

Translated 'praying' here, paired with ⲛⲏⲥⲧⲓⲁ 'fasting' throughout this kephalaion. While accumulated vocab tentatively suggests ⲡⲉϩⲱⲗⲏⲛ might mean 'his struggle,' the present context (paralleled three times with fasting and once described as 'the prayer that he prayed' — ⲡⲱⲗⲏⲛ ⲉⲧⲁϩⲱⲗⲏⲛ, line 3) decisively fixes it as 'pray/prayer.' This refines the prior tentative reading.
'The releaser' (already in glossary) — agentive of ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release.' Here functions as the cosmic figure attending the catechumen's first works, conveying their release.

Rendered 'body of light' rather than 'abode of light' or 'ship of light.' The accumulated tentative reading 'the abode' is here refined: the works are received ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ 'inward' into this entity, which is then qualified ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'of the gods.' The cosmic Body of Light (the divine soma into which freed light-particles are gathered) fits Manichaean technical usage. Could also be 'vessel of light.'
Read as 'the gods' (Lycopolitan plural of ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ); the genitive ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛ qualifies the body of light as belonging to the divine beings. Alternative: a verbal form 'they open.' Confidence moderate.

ⲭⲁⲗⲭ in glossary = 'mingle, fashion together' — here in the negative-cosmic register: the first works dwell within things 'while bound, while mingled' (i.e. entangled in matter). Pairs with ⲉⲩⲙⲣ̄ 'while bound.'

ⲟⲱ rendered 'stay/remain' (Lyc reflex possibly of ⲱϩⲉ 'stand' or ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'remain'). With negation ⲉⲛ + ⲍⲓⲃⲁⲗ 'outside' = 'do not stay outside.' The works do not remain external to the catechumen waiting; they are intrinsic to him until bodily death.
ⲥⲁⲙⲧ = qualitative of ⲥⲱⲙⲧ 'look out, watch, await' (Crum). 'Watching for him' fits the imagery: works do not wait outside the man.
= ⲧϭⲟⲙ 'the power' with assimilation. Standard Lycopolitan/scribal contraction.

= 'his comitatus' — Latin comitatus via Greek κομιτᾶτον (already in glossary). In this parable the comitatus is the imperial-style retinue of the man going to a city: it represents the catechumen's works being assembled in advance of his arrival.

Translated 'Inasmuch as the All' — taking ⲉⲡⲍⲟⲥⲟⲛ as Greek ἐφ' ὅσον 'as long as / inasmuch as,' with ⲁ- as directional preposition before ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄. ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ retained as 'the All' (cosmic-Manichaean term per glossary), here functioning as the kingly subject of the parable.
Read as ϣⲁⲕ-ϭⲛ̄ (habitual 2sg + ϭⲓⲛⲉ 'find'), with the unusual ϶ symbol representing ϭ. Generalizing 2nd person 'you find' fits the parable's didactic frame.
Standard Coptic idiom ϩⲁ-ϯ-ⲣⲁⲧ⸗ 'set foot.' The † here represents ϯ ('give'); ⲉ-ϩⲁ-ϯ-ⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ = 'to set his foot' = 'to set out on the road.'

Tentatively rendered 'they are able to be seen in advance before him' — ϣ-ⲛⲉⲩ as middle/passive 'be visible' or absolute 'be able to see.' Captures the parable's logic that the chosen members appear at the firmaments before the catechumen himself arrives. Confidence moderate; alternative 'they precede him in seeing' is possible.

Rendered 'they tarry' on contextual grounds (the third class of comitatus-members spend many days and months walking behind). Lexeme of uncertain root; possibly cognate with ϣⲱϥⲧ̄ 'be wearied' or related temporal-extension verb. Tentative.

Lycopolitan reflexive/intensive ϩⲱⲱϥ 'himself' (per dialect note in instructions). Renders the catechumen's own departure from the body as the temporal anchor for the second class of releasing members.

Translated 'I have made (it) known to you' per glossary entry ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉ 'make known/reveal' (causative on ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ 'manifest' or ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'declare'). Distinct from ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'raise up' despite phonetic similarity.

Tentatively translated 'raising (him) up,' analyzing as ⲉϥ-ⲧⲁⲗⲟ (circumstantial + ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise'). The form is irregular but the soteriological-vertical context (ten angels conveying the soul ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'upward' to the country of the Living) supports a raising-verb. Alternative: ⲉϥ-ⲧⲗⲟ 'while he ceases (= dies),' giving 'at his ceasing' = at the moment of death.
